source_type: device measurement/technical evaluation study (clinical-use device sampling, non-interventional)
laser_device: Low-power (low-level) laser photobiomodulation devices, 830 nm and 904 nm; specific diode type unspecified
hazard_studied: Deviation of actual laser power output and beam diameter from manufacturer-declared values, affecting treatment accuracy and reliability
parameter_or_operator_factor: Power output and beam diameter (device-side output parameters, measured across device age/use, not operator technique)
adverse_outcome: No direct patient harm reported; measured power output ranged from 2% to 134% of manufacturer-declared values and beam diameter varied 38% to 543% from nominal values, indicating output inconsistency
relevance_to_project: Provides precedent evidence that laser device power/beam output can drift substantially from stated or preset values with age and clinical use, supporting the rationale for verifying preset/power/speed reliability in an ex-vivo diode-laser study, though the devices studied are general low-level PBM units rather than dental cutting/soft-tissue diode lasers.

source_type: in vitro study (cell culture, human gingival fibroblasts)
laser_device: 940 nm continuous-wave diode laser (Epic X, Biolase)
hazard_studied: Not framed as a hazard/injury study; examines dose-dependent cellular bioenergetic and migratory responses of oral soft-tissue (gingival) fibroblasts to varying diode laser energy densities during photobiomodulation
parameter_or_operator_factor: Energy density of laser irradiation (6.49, 8.84, and 14.92 J/cm²) — a delivered-output/dose parameter
adverse_outcome: No adverse outcome reported in the available abstract; study reports dose-dependent changes in fibroblast metabolic activity, migration, nitric oxide production, and ATP levels (generally framed as beneficial/PBM effects, not injury)
relevance_to_project: Directly relevant as it uses the same laser type (940 nm diode) and a dose/output parameter (energy density) on oral soft-tissue cells, offering a parameter-outcome framework applicable to an ex-vivo diode-laser oral soft-tissue study, though it addresses therapeutic PBM dose-response rather than thermal injury or hazard specifically.

source_type: ex vivo experimental study (extracted immature teeth) with in vitro biocompatibility testing (stem cells from apical papilla)
hazard_studied: Thermal injury to external root surface and structural damage to internal root walls of immature teeth from diode laser irradiation during (biomimetic) endodontic treatment
parameter_or_operator_factor: Output power (0.5 W, 1 W, 1.5 W, 2 W) in continuous mode, irradiation time (5 s over four cycles) — power level directly linked to thermal/structural damage, with root wall thickness as an interacting factor
adverse_outcome: Temperature rise on external root surface correlated directly with higher output power and thinner root walls; study concludes 1 W is safe for immature teeth (with 1.5 W conditionally safe), implying higher powers risk thermal damage
relevance_to_project: Highly relevant: an ex vivo 940 nm diode-laser study directly and explicitly linking output power to thermal/structural tissue damage, closely paralleling the project's own ex-vivo power-parameter safety design, though focused on root/hard tissue rather than oral soft tissue.

source_type: technical characterization study with ex vivo experimental component (porcine tissue)
hazard_studied: Thermal damage zones and tissue cutting depth as a function of laser output parameters during contact-mode use
parameter_or_operator_factor: Output power (2-8 W average, up to 12.7 W CW, peak >30 W), pulse duration (5 µs to 1 ms), duty cycle (15-90%), and cut/movement speed (3 mm/s) — parameters directly linked to cutting depth and thermal damage zone size
adverse_outcome: Cuts of up to 1 mm depth with associated thermal damage zones were produced and measured on porcine tissue; no clinical adverse event, but a direct parameter-to-tissue-damage relationship was characterized
relevance_to_project: Highly relevant as a diode-laser technical characterization study directly linking power, pulse duration, duty cycle, and movement speed to tissue cutting depth and thermal damage zone, methodologically analogous to an ex-vivo diode-laser oral soft-tissue preset/power/speed reliability study, though the wavelength (445 nm) and tissue (porcine, non-oral) differ from a typical dental 940 nm oral soft-tissue setup.
